comments.text: The way you save this island is to leave it tf alone . People always messing with stuff. Honestly the question is why did this island grow and survive the way it did ?, keep in mind we all were 1

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That isolation really is the whole story - millions of years cut off from the mainland let evolution take its own strange path there, largely untouched by outside pressure until relatively recently.

comments.author: @cindyclayArt
comments.text: The Endemic genetics of Socotra is Amazing!   Beautiful & unreal looking!!   The Location & Greed may doom it quicker than goats. 🐐

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Fair worry - human development pressure often does move faster than any natural threat the island has faced before. Thank you for watching.

comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: Fascinating in so many ways, especially the geological information which makes what follows logical if not inevitable. As you say, a non-volcanic Galapagos. Shame that it seems to be caught up in the hostilities of the region. The various scripts in the cave are so interesting! The photography of plant and animal life is superb.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Thank you - "non-volcanic Galapagos" is a great way to put it, and that ancient script in the caves is one of the more mysterious threads in the whole story. Glad the photography did the place justice.
